examples.en: I paint watercolors every weekend.
For watercolors, you mix in a lot of water.
The watercolor hanging on the wall is really pretty.
I painted a seascape in watercolor.
Watercolor paint spreads easily.
I want to learn both watercolor and oil painting.

explain: 물에 푼 물감으로 그리는 그림을 가리켜요. 기름 물감으로 그리는 그림은 '유화'라고 해요. 그린다고 말할 때는 '수채화를 그리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I bought watercolor paints at the stationery shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림을 그리는 재료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the paint used for the art.

phrases.en: The rainy street looks like a watercolor painting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍경이 부드럽고 맑아 보일 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A comparison for soft, gentle-looking scenery.

phrases.en: I'm learning watercolor painting at a culture center these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미로 배우는 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about learning it as a hobby.

explain_en: It refers to a painting made with paint thinned in water. A painting made with oil paint is '유화'. To say you paint one, use '수채화를 그리다'.

examples.en: I can hear organ music in the church.
My older sister knows how to play the organ.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 오르간으로 치면 더 따뜻하게 들려요.
examples.en: That song sounds warmer when played on the organ.
The organ and the piano have similar keyboards.
We had the wedding at a cathedral that has an organ.
I like the piano more than the organ.

explain: 오르간과 피아노는 둘 다 건반이 있지만 소리가 달라요. 오르간도 피아노처럼 '오르간을 치다'라고 말해요. 학교 교실에 있던 작은 건반 악기는 '풍금'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 일주일에 한 번 오르간을 배워요.
phrases.en: I learn the organ once a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 배울 때 '을/를 배우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '을/를 배우다' when learning an instrument.

phrases.en: I listened to an organ performance at church.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르간으로 하는 연주를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a performance played on the organ.

phrases.en: My organ teacher is very kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오르간을 가르치는 사람을 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for the person who teaches you the organ.

explain_en: The organ and the piano both have keyboards, but the sound is different. You say '오르간을 치다', just like '피아노를 치다'. The small keyboard instrument that used to be in classrooms is sometimes called '풍금'.

examples.en: Grandmother sings while playing the janggu.
There is a janggu in the room.

examples.ko: 장구는 양쪽 면을 쳐서 소리를 내요.
examples.en: A janggu makes sound when you hit its two sides.

examples.ko: 학교 동아리에서 장구도 배우고 노래도 불러요.
examples.en: In the school club I learn the janggu and sing too.
Make a lively rhythm with the janggu.
In samulnori, people dance to the janggu.

explain: 한국 전통 악기로, 가운데가 잘록한 모양의 북이에요. 양쪽 면을 쳐서 소리를 내요. 사물놀이에서 쓰는 악기 중 하나예요.

phrases.en: I am learning how to play the janggu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북처럼 두드리는 악기는 '치다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Drum-like instruments use the verb 치다.

phrases.en: I can hear the janggu sound from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기가 내는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sound the instrument makes.

phrases.en: We danced to the janggu rhythm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장단'은 우리 음악의 리듬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 장단 is the rhythm pattern of Korean music.

explain_en: It is a traditional Korean drum with a narrow waist in the middle. You hit both sides to make sound. It is one of the instruments used in samulnori.

examples.en: My older brother plays the clarinet in the school band.
I like the clarinet because its sound is soft.
A clarinet makes sound when you blow into it with your mouth.
The new clarinet arrived, and I started practicing.
I tried playing movie music on the clarinet.

examples.ko: 클라리넷도 불고 피아노도 칠 줄 아는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who can play both the clarinet and the piano.

explain: 입으로 불어서 소리를 내는 악기라 '클라리넷을 불다'라고 해요. 피아노나 기타는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'를 써요. 외래어 표기는 '클라리네트'가 아니라 '클라리넷'이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 일주일에 두 번 클라리넷을 불어요.
phrases.en: I play the clarinet twice a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입으로 부는 악기라서 '불다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 불다 because you blow into it.

phrases.en: I can hear the soft sound of the clarinet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the instrument's sound.

phrases.en: I've been learning the clarinet since this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 공부한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying an instrument.

explain_en: You make the sound by blowing, so you say '클라리넷을 불다'. For piano and guitar you use '치다' and for violin '켜다'. The standard spelling is 클라리넷, not '클라리네트'.

examples.ko: 핸드볼은 손으로 공을 던져 골을 넣어요.
examples.en: In handball, you throw the ball by hand to score goals.
I played handball for the first time at school.
I watched a handball match on TV.
My younger sibling says they want to be a handball player.
Handball has goals like soccer does.

examples.ko: 체육 시간에 핸드볼로 반 대항전을 했어요.
examples.en: In gym class we had a handball match between classes.

explain: 스포츠 종목 이름이에요. 축구에서 손으로 공을 건드리는 반칙도 '핸드볼'이라고 해서 '핸드볼 반칙'이라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I watched a handball game in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 시합을 말할 때 '경기'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 경기 refers to a match.

phrases.en: My friend is a handball player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 핸드볼을 하는 선수를 말해요. 학교나 팀에서 뛰는 사람에게도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who plays handball on a team, at school or professionally.

phrases.en: We played handball in PE class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 이름 뒤에 '하다'를 붙여 그 운동을 한다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 after a sport's name means to play it.

explain_en: It is the name of a sport. In soccer, touching the ball with the hand is also called 핸드볼, so people sometimes say '핸드볼 반칙' (handball foul).

examples.en: I shave in front of the mirror every morning.
Yesterday I had no time, so I shaved in a rush.

examples.ko: 내일 면접이 있어서 일찍 면도할 거예요.
examples.en: I have an interview tomorrow, so I'll shave early.
My face stung while I was shaving.
I shaved and then put on lotion.
You look clean-faced because you shaved.

explain: '면도기', '면도날', '면도크림'처럼 도구 이름에도 '면도'가 들어가요. 수염과 얼굴 털을 밀 때 쓰고, 머리카락을 짧게 자를 때는 '자르다', '깎다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 이틀에 한 번 면도를 해요.
phrases.en: I shave once every two days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '면도하다'를 '면도를 하다'로 나눠 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The split form of 면도하다.

phrases.en: I shaved with a new razor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 나타내는 '으로'와 같이 쓰면 방법이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the tool with '으로' makes the method clear.

phrases.en: I was busy today, so I didn't shave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 하지 않은 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for saying you did not shave.

explain_en: The word 면도 also appears in tool names like 면도기, 면도날, and 면도크림. It is used for shaving a beard or facial hair, while cutting hair short uses 자르다 or 깎다.

examples.en: I tried to find constellations in the night sky.
My star sign is Pisces.

examples.ko: 별자리가 잘 보이는 곳으로 캠핑 갔어요.
examples.en: We went camping where the constellations are easy to see.
I checked my horoscope with a friend.
The stories about constellations are fun.
In the old days, people told direction by the constellations.

explain: '무슨 별자리예요?'는 하늘의 별이 아니라 생일로 정해지는 별자리를 묻는 말로 나와요. 운세 이야기를 할 때 많이 물어요.

phrases.en: I check my horoscope every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생일로 정해지는 별자리로 보는 운세를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fortune based on your birthday star sign.

phrases.en: What's your star sign? I'm a Leo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 생일 별자리를 물을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A question used to ask someone's birthday star sign.

phrases.en: You can see the constellations well here at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하늘의 별자리를 볼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for seeing constellations in the night sky.

explain_en: 'Museun byeoljariyeyo?' asks your star sign, which is set by your birthday, not a pattern in the sky. It comes up when people talk about horoscopes.

examples.en: I caught a crucian carp in the pond.
A crucian carp jumped above the water.
This crucian carp is as big as a palm.
The children fed the crucian carp.

examples.ko: 붕어로 만든 찜이 유명한 식당에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a restaurant famous for braised crucian carp.
They sell crucian carp at the market too.

explain: 붕어 모양 간식 '붕어빵'에는 붕어가 들어가지 않아요. 연못이나 강에 사는 민물고기라서 낚시나 매운탕 이야기에도 나와요.

phrases.en: looks just like (one's parent)
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족끼리 얼굴이 똑같이 닮았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when family members look exactly alike.

explain_en: The fish-shaped snack 붕어빵 contains no 붕어. It is a freshwater fish of ponds and rivers, so it comes up in talk about fishing and 매운탕.

examples.en: Tigers hunt at night.
People in the old days hunted animals with bows.
I saw a lion hunting on television.

examples.ko: 독수리가 토끼를 사냥할 때 정말 빨라요.
examples.en: An eagle is really fast when it hunts a rabbit.
My grandfather hunted in the mountains when he was young.

examples.ko: 이 동물은 무리를 지어 사냥해서 먹이를 구해요.
examples.en: This animal hunts in a group to find food.

explain: 사람도 동물도 먹이를 잡을 때 '사냥하다'를 써요. '사냥을 가다', '사냥을 나가다'처럼 '사냥'과 다른 동사를 같이 써도 돼요. 낚시로 물고기를 잡을 때는 '낚시하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My father went hunting in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사냥'을 명사로 쓰고 '가다'와 같이 말해요. 사냥하러 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here '사냥' is a noun used with '가다'. It means going out to hunt.

phrases.en: Wolves hunt rabbits and eat them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어서'로 두 동작을 이어요. 동물이 먹이를 구하는 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-a/eoseo' links two actions. It is common when talking about animals getting food.

phrases.en: The hunter went into the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사냥을 하는 사람을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This noun refers to a person who hunts.

explain_en: Both people and animals '사냥하다' when they catch prey. You can also use the noun with another verb, as in '사냥을 가다' or '사냥을 나가다'. Catching fish with a rod is '낚시하다'.

en: to be moved (physically); to be relocated

examples.en: The file was moved to another folder.
The luggage is moved onto the truck.
The patient is being taken to the hospital.
Let's restart from the new position.

examples.ko: 사진이 다른 곳으로 이동될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: The photos may be moved elsewhere.
The desk has been moved to the window.

explain: 사람이 걸어가는 게 아니라 물건, 자료, 환자처럼 다른 힘으로 옮겨질 때 써요. 내가 직접 가는 건 '이동하다'를 써요. 컴퓨터에서 파일을 옮겼다고 할 때도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Photos are automatically moved to the album.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 앱에서 파일이나 자료가 옮겨질 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when files or data move on a computer or app.

phrases.en: The file hasn't been moved yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옮겨지지 않은 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something that has not been moved.

phrases.en: The patient was taken to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이동되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 이동되다 and more common in daily conversation.

explain_en: Used when things like objects, data or a patient are moved by some other force, not when a person walks. When you go by yourself, the active verb is used. It also comes up often for files being moved on a computer.

p.n: 이전되다 is for offices or institutions, so it sounds odd for furniture.

examples.en: We bought a new rice cooker for our newlywed home.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥이 밥이 다 됐다고 알려 줘요.
examples.en: The rice cooker tells me the rice is done.
You can also steam food with a rice cooker.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥에 쌀과 물을 넣고 취사 버튼을 눌렀어요.
examples.en: I put rice and water in the rice cooker and pressed the cook button.
This rice cooker keeps food warm for a long time.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥 뚜껑을 열자 김이 확 올라왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the rice cooker lid, steam rushed up.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '밥솥'이라고 해도 통해요. 버튼은 '취사'(밥 짓기)와 '보온'(따뜻하게 두기)이 기본이에요. 밥을 '짓다'라고 하는 점도 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: I put rice in the rice cooker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '전기밥솥'을 줄여서 '밥솥'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, '전기밥솥' is shortened to '밥솥'.

phrases.en: I cook rice with an electric rice cooker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥은 '하다'가 아니라 '짓다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For rice, you say '짓다' rather than '하다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to cook rice in a rice cooker

phrases.en: The rice cooker broke, so I bought a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 망가졌을 때 '고장 나다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '고장 나다' when a machine breaks.

explain_en: In daily life, just saying '밥솥' also works. The basic buttons are '취사' (cook) and '보온' (keep warm). Also note that rice is 'made' with the verb '짓다'.

examples.en: I turn left at the next signal.
The car in front suddenly turned left.
If you turn left at that intersection, you will see a bank.
Many cars are turning left, so the road is jammed.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 들어서 좌회전할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I took a wrong road and could not turn left.
Turn left and go just two blocks, and you will arrive.

explain: 반대말은 '우회전하다'예요. 좌회전은 주로 차를 몰 때 써요. 걸어서 길을 알려 줄 때는 '왼쪽으로 가세요'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Please turn left at the intersection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 알려 주거나 운전하는 사람에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving directions to a driver.

phrases.en: If you turn left and go a bit, there is a bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해서'로 이어서 다음 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -해서 form links to the next step in directions.

phrases.en: The left-turn signal came on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '좌회전'을 명사처럼 써서 신호와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here 좌회전 works as a noun paired with 신호.

explain_en: Its opposite is 우회전하다. It is mainly for driving. When giving walking directions, 왼쪽으로 가세요 sounds more natural.

examples.en: There is a small globe on the desk.

examples.ko: 지구본을 돌리면서 가고 싶은 나라를 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I spun the globe and looked for countries I want to visit.
I bought a globe as a birthday present for my child.

examples.ko: 지구본으로 보면 한국과 브라질이 얼마나 먼지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: On a globe you can see how far apart Korea and Brazil are.

examples.ko: 지구본은 세계 지도보다 실제 모양에 더 가까워요.
examples.en: A globe is closer to the real shape than a world map.
Shall we try finding our country on this globe?

explain: 평평한 '세계 지도'와 달리 둥근 모양이라 나라의 크기와 거리를 더 실제에 가깝게 볼 수 있어요. 보통 '지구본을 돌리다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I spun the globe and found Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지구본을 쓰는 가장 흔한 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common action done with a globe.

phrases.en: I study country names with a globe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지구본을 도구로 쓸 때 '으로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 으로 when the globe is a tool or means.

phrases.en: On the globe, Korea looks very small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지구본 위에서 무엇을 찾거나 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when finding or seeing something on the globe.

explain_en: Unlike a flat '세계 지도' (world map), the round shape shows country sizes and distances closer to reality. The usual collocation is '지구본을 돌리다' (to spin the globe).
